questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which branch of biology studies plants?
questions.answer: Botany

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: How is biochemistry related to biology?
questions.answer: Biochemistry explains the chemical substances and reactions that occur in living organisms.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain how biology connects with at least three other sciences.
questions.answer: Award marks for three valid links such as biochemistry with chemistry, biophysics with physics, biostatistics/computational biology with mathematics or computing, plus a clear explanation of why interdisciplinary study improves biological understanding.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.topic_name: Scientific method and biological problem solving
questions.question_text: What is a hypothesis?

options.text: A random guess that cannot be tested

questions.answer: A testable proposed explanation
tags: Scientific method and biological problem solving

questions.subject: Biology
questions.topic_name: Scientific method and biological problem solving
questions.question_text: Why must a scientific hypothesis be testable?
questions.answer: It must allow observations or experiments that can support or refute the proposed explanation.
tags: Scientific method and biological problem solving

questions.subject: Biology
questions.topic_name: Scientific method and biological problem solving
questions.question_text: Describe the main steps of the biological method from observation to conclusion.
questions.answer: Award marks for observation/problem identification, hypothesis, deductions/predictions, experimentation/data collection, and conclusion with possible revision of the hypothesis.
tags: Scientific method and biological problem solving

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which taxonomic rank is more specific than genus?
questions.answer: Species

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Why is biological classification useful?
questions.answer: It organizes biodiversity, helps identify organisms, and allows scientists to communicate about relationships and differences systematically.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain the purpose of taxonomic ranks and arrange the major ranks from broad to specific.
questions.answer: Award marks for purpose of classification and correct sequence from domain/kingdom through phylum, class, order, family, genus and species, with recognition that lower ranks are more specific.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: In binomial nomenclature, how many words make up a scientific species name?
questions.answer: Two

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: State the basic rule for writing a binomial scientific name.
questions.answer: It contains the genus name followed by the specific epithet; the genus begins with a capital letter and both words are conventionally italicized or underlined when handwritten.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Compare the three-domain system and explain why viruses are treated differently in classification.
questions.answer: Award marks for naming Bacteria, Archaea and Eukarya, noting cellular organization differences, and explaining that viruses are acellular and depend on host cells for replication.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.topic_name: Cell as the basic unit of life
questions.question_text: Which statement best describes the cell?

options.text: The basic structural and functional unit of life

questions.answer: The basic structural and functional unit of life
tags: Cell as the basic unit of life

questions.subject: Biology
questions.topic_name: Cell as the basic unit of life
questions.question_text: State two ideas of cell theory.
questions.answer: Living organisms are made of cells, and the cell is the basic unit of structure and function; new cells arise from pre-existing cells.
tags: Cell as the basic unit of life

questions.subject: Biology
questions.topic_name: Cell as the basic unit of life
questions.question_text: Explain how cell theory links microscopic observations with the organization of living organisms.
questions.answer: Award marks for organisms being cellular, cell as basic unit, cells arising from existing cells, evidence from microscopy, and relation of cells to tissues/organs.
tags: Cell as the basic unit of life

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which organelle contains most of a eukaryotic cell’s genetic material?
questions.answer: Nucleus

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Give two differences between typical plant and animal cells.
questions.answer: Plant cells typically have a cellulose cell wall and chloroplasts/large central vacuole; animal cells lack a cell wall and chloroplasts.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Compare the functions of nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, cell membrane and chloroplasts.
questions.answer: Award one mark for each correct function: genetic control, aerobic energy release, protein synthesis, selective exchange, and photosynthesis respectively.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is the main result of mitosis?

options.text: One cell with half the chromosome number

questions.answer: Two genetically similar daughter cells

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Why is mitosis important for growth?
questions.answer: It increases cell number while maintaining chromosome number and genetic continuity in body tissues.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Describe the role of the cell cycle and mitosis in growth and tissue repair.
questions.answer: Award marks for interphase preparation/DNA replication, chromosome separation in mitosis, cytokinesis, maintenance of chromosome number, and contribution to growth/repair.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What happens to chromosome number during meiosis?

options.text: It is reduced by half in the products
It never changes from the parent cell

questions.answer: It is reduced by half in the products

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: State one way meiosis differs from mitosis.
questions.answer: Meiosis involves two divisions and produces haploid cells with genetic variation, while mitosis produces two genetically similar cells with the same chromosome number as the parent.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain how meiosis supports sexual reproduction and genetic variation.
questions.answer: Award marks for chromosome-number reduction, formation of gametes, two divisions, genetic variation through recombination/independent assortment, and restoration of diploid number at fertilization.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which sequence is correct from simpler to more complex?
questions.answer: Cell → tissue → organ → organ system

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Differentiate tissue and organ.
questions.answer: A tissue is a group of similar cells performing related functions; an organ contains multiple tissues working together for a larger function.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain levels of biological organization using one plant or human example.
questions.answer: Award marks for cell, tissue, organ, organ system and organism levels, plus a logically linked example such as muscle cell → muscle tissue → heart → circulatory system.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is homeostasis?

options.text: Maintenance of relatively stable internal conditions

questions.answer: Maintenance of relatively stable internal conditions

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Why is homeostasis important for cells?
questions.answer: Stable internal conditions help enzymes and cellular processes operate within suitable ranges despite external changes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain how organ systems cooperate to maintain homeostasis.
questions.answer: Award marks for concept of stable internal environment and coordinated roles of at least four systems such as circulatory transport, respiratory gas exchange, urinary regulation, nervous/endocrine control, or skin/temperature regulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which biomolecule is a major immediate source of cellular energy?
questions.answer: Carbohydrate

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: State one major role of proteins and one of lipids.
questions.answer: Proteins can act as enzymes or structural/transport molecules; lipids store energy and are important in membranes and insulation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Compare carbohydrates, proteins and lipids in terms of building components and biological roles.
questions.answer: Award marks for monomers/components and key roles: sugars/polysaccharides for energy/structure, amino acids/proteins for enzymes/structure, and fatty acids/glycerol-based lipids for energy storage/membranes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which nucleic acid stores most hereditary information?
questions.answer: DNA

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: How are DNA and RNA related to protein production?
questions.answer: DNA stores genetic instructions; RNA carries or helps interpret those instructions during protein synthesis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain the flow of genetic information from DNA to a functional protein.
questions.answer: Award marks for gene/DNA information, transcription to RNA, RNA movement/function, translation at ribosomes, and amino-acid sequence forming a functional protein.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is the main role of an enzyme?

options.text: To speed a specific biochemical reaction without being consumed

questions.answer: To speed a specific biochemical reaction without being consumed

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is meant by enzyme specificity?
questions.answer: An enzyme’s active site fits particular substrate(s), so it catalyzes only certain reactions or closely related reactions.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Describe the enzyme-substrate mechanism and why enzymes can be reused.
questions.answer: Award marks for active site, substrate binding, enzyme-substrate complex, product formation/release, and enzyme remaining chemically available for another cycle.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which factor can change enzyme activity by altering molecular motion and protein shape?
questions.answer: Temperature

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Why can very high temperature reduce enzyme activity?
questions.answer: High temperature can disrupt the enzyme’s three-dimensional structure and active site, reducing substrate binding and catalysis.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain how temperature, pH, substrate concentration and inhibitors can affect enzyme activity.
questions.answer: Award marks for each factor’s effect and a final explanation that enzyme activity depends on collisions/active-site structure and availability.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is ATP mainly used for in cells?

options.text: Permanent storage of all hereditary information

questions.answer: Short-term transfer of usable energy

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Why is ATP called an energy currency of the cell?
questions.answer: Cells can form ATP when energy is available and hydrolyze it to transfer manageable amounts of energy to cellular processes.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain the ATP-ADP cycle and how it links energy-releasing and energy-requiring reactions.
questions.answer: Award marks for ATP formation from ADP + phosphate, energy storage, ATP hydrolysis, coupling to cellular work, and recycling of ADP.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which process captures light energy to build organic molecules?
questions.answer: Photosynthesis

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: How are photosynthesis and cellular respiration related?
questions.answer: Photosynthesis stores energy in organic molecules using carbon dioxide and water, while respiration releases usable energy by breaking down organic molecules; their reactants/products are broadly complementary.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Compare photosynthesis and cellular respiration in terms of purpose, main inputs, main outputs and cellular location.
questions.answer: Award marks for purpose, inputs/outputs and correct locations such as chloroplasts for photosynthesis and mitochondria for most aerobic respiration.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which tissue mainly transports water and mineral salts upward in plants?
questions.answer: Xylem

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Differentiate xylem and phloem transport.
questions.answer: Xylem mainly carries water/mineral ions from roots upward; phloem translocates organic nutrients such as sucrose between sources and sinks.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain how roots, xylem and phloem cooperate in plant nutrition and transport.
questions.answer: Award marks for root absorption, xylem water/mineral transport, photosynthetic production of sugars, phloem translocation, and source-sink relationship.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is transpiration?

options.text: Loss of water vapour from aerial plant surfaces, mainly through stomata
Movement of sugar in phloem only

questions.answer: Loss of water vapour from aerial plant surfaces, mainly through stomata

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: State one benefit and one cost of transpiration.
questions.answer: It helps pull water/minerals upward and can cool leaves, but excessive water loss can cause wilting or water stress.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Explain how stomata participate in both gaseous exchange and water regulation.
questions.answer: Award marks for stomatal pores, CO2 entry, O2/water-vapour exit, guard-cell regulation, and balance between photosynthesis and water conservation.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which feature is typical of asexual reproduction?

options.text: One parent and no fusion of gametes
Fusion of two gametes is required
Chromosome number must double every generation

questions.answer: One parent and no fusion of gametes

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is artificial vegetative propagation?
questions.answer: It is deliberate production of new plants from vegetative parts using methods such as cuttings, grafting or layering.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Compare natural asexual reproduction with artificial propagation in plants.
questions.answer: Award marks for one-parent/no-gamete-fusion concept, examples of natural methods, examples of artificial methods, genetic similarity of offspring, and agricultural advantages/limitations.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What process transfers pollen from anther to stigma?
questions.answer: Pollination

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Differentiate pollination and fertilization.
questions.answer: Pollination is transfer of pollen to a stigma; fertilization is fusion of male and female gamete nuclei after pollen-tube growth.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Describe the sequence from pollination to seed and fruit formation in a flowering plant.
questions.answer: Award marks for pollination, pollen germination/tube growth, fertilization, zygote/embryo and seed formation, and ovary/fruit development.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: What is the arithmetic mean?

options.text: Sum of observations divided by number of observations

questions.answer: Sum of observations divided by number of observations

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Differentiate median and mode.
questions.answer: Median is the middle value when data are ordered; mode is the value occurring most frequently.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: For a biological dataset, explain how mean, median and mode provide different summaries.
questions.answer: Award marks for correct definition of each measure, one contrast between them, an example of when each may be informative, and recognition that unusual values can affect the mean strongly.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Which graph is appropriate for comparing counts across discrete categories?
questions.answer: Bar chart

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: State two features of a well-constructed bar chart.
questions.answer: It should have labelled axes with an appropriate scale/categories and separate bars of consistent width; a clear title is also useful.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question_text: Describe how to organize and present categorical biological data in a bar chart.
questions.answer: Award marks for identifying categories, calculating/recording frequencies, choosing a suitable scale, drawing labelled separate bars, and adding clear title/axis labels.
